newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ECON MIN WARNS OF CONSERVATIVE POPULISM.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ECON MIN WARNS OF CONSERVATIVE POPULISM.

text.p: Traditional Greek stereotypes of free-spending socialists and economically mean conservatives have been reversed in the campaign for national elections in two weeks.
Now it's the opposition conservatives who are talking about generous handouts and the ruling socialists who warn voters that further sacrifices are needed to meet EU economic targets.
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said on Monday that conservative populism would widen Greece's budget deficit and would lose out to the socialist's prudent economic policy.

"If (conservative) New Democracy wins they will add about 3.0 percent to the budget deficit in terms of GDP and this will take us back to the position they handed over (to us) in 1993," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"We hope that the Greek people will reward prudence and responsibility," he said, adding the socialists under Premier Costas Simitis will adhere to the EU convergence programme.
The conservatives, tempting farmers and small business with populist promises, are neck-and-neck with the socialists less than two weeks before elections, according to opinion polls.
A weekend MRB poll showed voters are split with 31 percent favouring the conservatives led by Miltiadis Evert and 30.6 percent preferring the socialists.

Papandoniou said no new taxes were planned to boost state revenues but greater effectiveness in tax collection would yield substantial dividends helped by the computerisation of the tax collection at the finance ministry.

"One of the more interesting successes of our economic policy is that we have been able to raise tax receipts without imposing new taxes or raising coefficients. We shall follow the same path with greater effectiveness," he said.
The government's year-end targets would put GDP growth at 2.6 percent, cut the budget deficit to 7.6 percent of GDP and hit an average inflation rate of 8.2 percent, just above target.
With good news for the bourse, the socialists are planning greater autonomy for the country's pension funds if they get a new four-year mandate.
Pension funds which are restricted to mainly treasuries will be allowed to invest assets in the bourse, which will help the socialists were plans for further part flotations of more state utilities.
Next in line after the successful part float of OTE telecoms is the Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP), he said.

"Our policy is to extend the ability of pension funds to gradually invest in stocks. This has become reality with shares of OTE telecoms and it is our intention to grant greater autonomy to pension funds," Papandoniou told RFTV.
Asked to comment on the socialist policy to set up private casinos, he said existing contracts would be implemented but there was no plan to expand the number of casinos.
"We are very conservative socially on gambling and casinos. We've made some limited inroads but do not plan to extend the area for casinos in Greece. We shall implement existing contracts," he said.

Papandoniou played down criticism from both the left and the right that the socialists were wedded to austerity, gradually abandoning the welfare state set up by the late party founder, Andreas Papandreou.
"We are a modern socialist party. Pasok (the socialist party) fully espouses the market economy, a liberal economy with limited government interference," he said.
